relevance_reason: Directly relevant: the paper reports a patient with OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome caused by a de novo heterozygous dominant-negative OTULIN variant. The findings were not extracted in this session because a safety classifier stopped the earlier response, so the paper needs manual or separate curation.

This is the first report of heterozygous de novo dominant negative OTULIN C129S variants causing an ORAS-like autoinflammatory disease, the subject of AIPDSA. It describes the clinical features of 2 patients, the variants, functional studies and treatment.

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) described a 22-month-old Caucasian boy (P1) with non-consanguineous parents who was born at 31 weeks' gestation. At 4 days of age he developed peri-umbilical erythema with sterile neutrophilic inflammation around a urachal remnant. After surgery the wound dehisced and failed to close, and he later developed a spontaneous cutaneous duodenal stoma. At 8 weeks he had an acute respiratory deterioration with body edema, hypotension and presumed pulmonary edema that responded to corticosteroids. He had recurrent panniculitis, pathergy with sterile pustular abscesses at injection and cannula sites, a tricuspid valve echogenic focus treated as culture-negative endocarditis, raised CRP (100-200 mg/L), neutrophilia, monocytosis, eosinophilia, persistent thrombocytopenia, initial hypogammaglobulinemia, and a skin biopsy showing acute inflammatory exudate with suppuration and necrosis.
quotes: The patient is a 22-mo-old male, born to non-consanguineous Caucasian parents. Born at 31 wk of gestation by emergency cesarean section for maternal eclampsia

he developed repeated areas of swelling and erythema consistent with panniculitis, and additionally developed lesions that were believed to represent pathergy, with sterile pustular abscesses forming at the sight of prior trauma

Investigations demonstrated raised inflammatory markers (C reactive protein [CRP] 100–200 mg/L) and elevated neutrophils (30–50 × 109/L), monocytes (2–10 × 109/L), eosinophilia (1–3 × 109/L), and a persistent thrombocytopaenia (below 100 × 109/L)

phenotypes.text: acute respiratory deterioration with pulmonary edema

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) described a Saudi girl (P2) born at term to non-consanguineous parents. At 7 months of age, 2 weeks after routine vaccinations, she presented with fever, generalized edema and multiple tender skin lesions that progressed to cellulitis-like plaques and necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration requiring debridement and fasciotomy. She had leukocytosis, neutrophilia and a high CRP (264 mg/L), all cultures were negative, and biopsy showed neutrophil and plasma cell infiltration with necrosis. At 12 months she had a second attack with fever, erythematous plaques, CRP 393 mg/L and skin biopsy showing panniculitis, and she responded promptly to corticosteroids.
quotes: She was asymptomatic until the age of 7 mo when she presented to a tertiary hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with multiple tender skin lesions over the upper and lower limbs bilaterally, associated with a fever (38–39°C) and generalized edema
some of her lesions progressed to a picture of tender cellulitis-like plaques evolving into necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration
Again, her initial investigations showed leukocytosis (19.9 × 109/L) with neutrophilia (12.9 × 109/L), very high CRP (393 mg/L), and negative cultures. Skin biopsy revealed panniculitis.

findings.statement: In P1, trio exome sequencing by Davidson et al. (2024) identified a de novo heterozygous c.386G>C variant in the OTULIN gene, resulting in a cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution. The variant was absent from gnomAD. Cys129 is part of the catalytic domain and is essential for OTULIN enzymatic activity.
quotes: Trio exome sequencing was performed on P1 and his parents; this identified a de novo variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.386G>C, resulting in a missense change from cysteine to serine at position 129 (p.Cys129Ser)
The C129S OTULIN variant was previously unreported and absent from databases of normal variation, including gnomAD (v2.1.1 and v3.1.2).
Significantly, cysteine 129 is part of the OTULIN catalytic domain and is essential for OTULIN enzymatic activity

findings.statement: In P2, whole-genome sequencing by Davidson et al. (2024) identified a heterozygous c.385T>A variant in the OTULIN gene that results in the same cys129-to-ser (C129S) substitution. Testing of the parents confirmed that it was de novo.
quotes: P2 underwent whole genome sequencing and a variant in OTULIN, ENST00000284274.5:c.385T>A, which results in the same cysteine to serine change at position 129, was identified.
Follow-up testing on P2’s parents confirmed the de novo nature of the variant

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S OTULIN had thermostability similar to wildtype and that OTULIN and LUBAC component levels were normal in patient fibroblasts. However, the mutant failed to hydrolyze M1-linked di-ubiquitin. An activity-based probe showed that wildtype (active) and C129S (inactive) OTULIN were coexpressed in roughly equal amounts in patient fibroblasts. Surface plasmon resonance showed that C129S OTULIN bound M1-di-ubiquitin with high affinity.
quotes: C129S OTULIN exhibited equivalent protein stability with similar melting temperature to wild type (WT) OTULIN in a Tycho NT.6 assay
C129S OTULIN, like the previously reported C129A mutation, failed to hydrolyze M1–di-Ub in a cell-free cleavage assay over a range of concentrations
we confirmed that in patient fibroblasts, both WT (active) and C129S (inactive) forms of OTULIN are coexpressed in seemingly equal amounts

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) observed accumulation of M1-linked ubiquitin chains in patient fibroblasts. Transfecting C129S OTULIN into HEK293T cells, which express endogenous OTULIN, caused M1-ubiquitin accumulation and dose-dependent NF-kappa-B activation. Wildtype OTULIN and the loss-of-function variants Y244C and N341D did not have these effects. C129S OTULIN drove NF-kappa-B activity even when cotransfected with wildtype at lower ratios, indicating a dominant negative effect.
quotes: we observed significant accumulation of M1-Ub chains in patient cells compared with HD fibroblasts

transient transfection of C129S OTULIN, but not WT OTULIN or two representative OTULIN loss-of-function mutants, N341D (Spaan et al., 2022) and Y244C (Zhou et al., 2016), triggered NFκB activity as assessed by luciferase assay
Collectively, these data indicate C129S OTULIN has a dominant negative effect over WT OTULIN and may thereby drive autoinflammatory disease, even in a heterozygous context.

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) found that C129S patient fibroblasts were as sensitive to TNF/cycloheximide-induced cell death as fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS, and more sensitive than fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients or healthy donors. The death was mainly apoptotic, because it was reduced by caspase inhibition and minimally affected by necrostatin-1. TNF-induced MAPK and NF-kappa-B signaling and IL-6/IL-8 secretion were largely normal in patient fibroblasts.
quotes: C129S heterozygous OTULIN and ORAS fibroblasts exhibited markedly increased sensitivity to TNF-induced cell death compared with HD and OTULIN-haploinsufficent cells
Thus, C129S heterozygous OTULIN patient fibroblasts die primarily by apoptosis and, to a lesser extent, by necroptosis in response to TNF+CHX stimulation.
this data demonstrates that C129S OTULIN heterozygosity does not significantly alter MAPK or NFκB signaling in response to TNF stimulation in patient fibroblasts

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) observed markedly increased transcription of IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF, in PBMCs from P1. P1's fibroblasts had an elevated interferon-stimulated gene score that was similar to fibroblasts from patients with biallelic ORAS and higher than in healthy donor and OTULIN-haploinsufficient fibroblasts. THP-1 monocytes stably expressing C129S OTULIN, but not wildtype OTULIN, showed a similar inflammatory gene signature.
quotes: we did identify a marked increase in transcription of proinflammatory cytokines, IFNB1 and IL6, and to a lesser extent TNF in the peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of P1
Consistent with elevated IFNB1 in patient cells, we also observed an elevated ISG Score compared with HDs and OTULIN-haploinsufficent lines
a similar inflammatory gene signature was observed in the human monocyte line, THP-1s cells upon stable expression of C129S OTULIN but not WT OTULIN

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) showed that C129S OTULIN binds LUBAC. In cells it promoted ubiquitination of LUBAC components SHARPIN and, to a lesser extent, HOIP. Patient fibroblasts showed increased OTULIN-LUBAC interaction, and most LUBAC-bound OTULIN was catalytically inactive. Patient cells also showed reduced recruitment of LUBAC (HOIP, SHARPIN) to the TNFR1 signaling complex and reduced RIPK1 modification. The authors concluded that accumulation of M1-ubiquitin on LUBAC reduces its recruitment to TNFR1 and promotes TNF-induced cell death, which leads to necrotizing tissue.
quotes: we confirmed that in C129S OTULIN patient cells, the majority of OTULIN bound to the LUBAC complex is catalytically inactive

Thus, C129S OTULIN heterozygosity leads to accumulation of M1-Ub chains on LUBAC complexes, which reduces LUBAC recruitment to the TNFR1 signaling complex. Decreased LUBAC recruitment promotes TNF-induced cell death
we observed reduced recruitment of LUBAC components SHARPIN and HOIP to the TNFR1 signaling complex in patient cells compared with HD and this was associated with reduced M1-Ub

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) reported that both patients responded to corticosteroids. P1 was treated with adalimumab, which allowed steroid reduction, lowered CRP and supported wound healing; ruxolitinib was also tried in P1, but its benefit was unclear. P2 was treated with infliximab plus methotrexate, was weaned off steroids and remained in remission for 2 years. Prophylactic antibiotics improved wound healing in P1 and controlled recurrent chest infections in P2.
quotes: In addition to steroids, he was treated with TNF-blockade (Adalimumab), which seemed to improve the rate of healing allowing for a reduced steroid dose, and JAK inhibition (Ruxolitinib).
the patient was started on anti-TNF (Infliximab) with adjunctive Methotrexate, and corticosteroid was successfully weaned off
she remains in clinical and biochemical remission since starting anti-TNF therapy, and she completed her third year of life in June 2023, achieving 2 years of disease remission

findings.statement: Davidson et al. (2024) reported the first heterozygous, dominant negative OTULIN variant to cause ORAS-like disease. It arose de novo in 2 unrelated individuals, in contrast to the previously reported biallelic loss-of-function variants.
quotes: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
This is the first report of ORAS-like disease caused by a heterozygous variant.
